key_insight: Syndrome records can be reused in classical post-processing to virtually cancel logical errors in universal quantum circuits, avoiding prior noise learning and circuit modification.
engineering_relevance: This enables bias-free logical error mitigation with lower experimental complexity, offering a practical path to more accurate early fault-tolerant quantum computations.
method: Use only syndrome records from logical circuit runs for post-processing.
Pair a fast experimental decoder with a more powerful offline decoder.
Apply dual-decoder virtual error cancellation to reduce logical error bias beyond syndrome-based postselection.
evidence_signal: In simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, the dual-decoder protocol showed error that decreased with more samples and achieved over three orders of magnitude suppression relative to the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable regime.
watch_item: The approach still depends on high-quality syndrome data and may incur substantial classical post-processing cost or decoder-mismatch sensitivity in practice.
paper_title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
